scenes.tts: The first film showed how a new genetic difference can begin. How can one mutation help in one setting but not another? Follow its effect. Keep the D N A fixed while the world moves around it.
scenes.caption: The first film showed how a new genetic difference can begin. How can one mutation help in one setting but not another? Follow its effect. Keep the DNA fixed while the world moves around it.
scenes.visual: Reuse the first film's COLOUR MAP exactly: inherited information BLUE; environment GREEN; mutation GOLD; a changed trait PURPLE; blocked route RED; other lines WHITE. A GOLD-corner allele card stays centred while the background moves from light to dark. A question mark tracks beside 'effect'.
scenes.narration: The first film showed how a new genetic difference can begin. How can one mutation help in one setting but not another? Follow its effect. Keep the DNA fixed while the world moves around it.

scenes.visual: The moving background continues behind the title 'When a Mutation Matters'. The title dissolves while the GOLD mutation marker remains fixed.

scenes.tts: A mutation does not come with a fixed label. Its effect depends on the change, and often on its environment. Start with colour. A label only makes sense beside a measured outcome.
scenes.caption: A mutation does not come with a fixed label. Its effect depends on the change, and often on its environment. Start with colour. A label only makes sense beside a measured outcome.
scenes.visual: The GOLD-corner allele card transforms into a PURPLE colour patch on a cartoon beetle. Three empty labels orbit it, then fade before attaching: 'helpful', 'harmful', 'no difference'. Leave the beetle unlabelled.
scenes.narration: A mutation does not come with a fixed label. Its effect depends on the change, and often on its environment. Start with colour. A label only makes sense beside a measured outcome.

scenes.tts: Place the beetle on a matching background. It is harder to notice there. Slide the same beetle onto a contrasting background. It becomes easier to notice. The model shows a possible effect, not a promised outcome.
scenes.caption: Place the beetle on a matching background. It is harder to notice there. Slide the same beetle onto a contrasting background. It becomes easier to notice. The model shows a possible effect, not a promised outcome.
scenes.visual: A PURPLE beetle walks across two large panels. On the matching panel its outline is faint; on the contrasting panel its outline is clear. The GOLD mutation marker never changes. Label the comparison 'schematic'; show an observing eye, not a predator attack.
scenes.narration: Place the beetle on a matching background. It is harder to notice there. Slide the same beetle onto a contrasting background. It becomes easier to notice. The model shows a possible effect, not a promised outcome.

scenes.tts: The D N A did not change during that move. The environment changed. A colour that affects survival one way here may act differently there. That separation is the key test.
scenes.caption: The DNA did not change during that move. The environment changed. A colour that affects survival one way here may act differently there. That separation is the key test.
scenes.visual: Pin the GOLD-corner allele card above both panels with a lock icon. Only the GREEN background slider moves. A two-headed WHITE arrow links 'effect here' and 'effect there', both ending in question marks rather than verdicts.
scenes.narration: The DNA did not change during that move. The environment changed. A colour that affects survival one way here may act differently there. That separation is the key test.

scenes.tts: Predict before the next move. If the background changes again, must the beetle's D N A change before the colour's effect changes? Hold your answer. Keep your eyes on the locked gold marker.
scenes.caption: Predict before the next move. If the background changes again, must the beetle's DNA change before the colour's effect changes? Hold your answer. Keep your eyes on the locked gold marker.
scenes.visual: Keep the beetle and locked GOLD allele card still. A GREEN background swatch waits at the edge. Question across the top: 'Must DNA change first?'
scenes.narration: Predict before the next move. If the background changes again, must the beetle's DNA change before the colour's effect changes? Hold your answer. Keep your eyes on the locked gold marker.

scenes.visual: Predict pause. The question stays. The beetle's legs move gently in place, the GOLD card glows, and the waiting GREEN swatch shimmers.

scenes.tts: No. Keep the mutation fixed and change only the setting. The effect can change because survival and reproduction happen in an environment, not outside one. The same change now meets different conditions.
scenes.caption: No. Keep the mutation fixed and change only the setting. The effect can change because survival and reproduction happen in an environment, not outside one. The same change now meets different conditions.
scenes.visual: The GREEN swatch slides behind the beetle. The locked GOLD card stays identical. A simple schematic survival-and-offspring gauge shifts without labels such as 'best', 'rejected', or 'extinct'.
scenes.narration: No. Keep the mutation fixed and change only the setting. The effect can change because survival and reproduction happen in an environment, not outside one. The same change now meets different conditions.

scenes.tts: Many mutations change little that matters for survival. Some harm how a protein works. A few can help under particular conditions. These are outcomes, not intentions. A mutation can also change how much protein a cell makes.
scenes.caption: Many mutations change little that matters for survival. Some harm how a protein works. A few can help under particular conditions. These are outcomes, not intentions. A mutation can also change how much protein a cell makes.
scenes.visual: Transform the beetle into three large labelled-block pathways, not molecular structures. A GOLD change leads to a wide pathway into an unchanged output meter, a medium pathway into a wobbling PURPLE protein block, or a thin pathway into improved growth under a named condition. Mark all three 'schematic'. A crossed-out target icon reinforces 'not intentions'.
scenes.narration: Many mutations change little that matters for survival. Some harm how a protein works. A few can help under particular conditions. These are outcomes, not intentions. A mutation can also change how much protein a cell makes.

scenes.tts: Bacteria make the same point. One mutation can allow growth with an antibiotic. Yet with different food, which mutant grows best can change. Food and the drug are both parts of the environment.
scenes.caption: Bacteria make the same point. One mutation can allow growth with an antibiotic. Yet with different food, which mutant grows best can change. Food and the drug are both parts of the environment.
scenes.visual: Keep one GOLD-corner bacterial allele card above two large culture panels. A dish labelled 'antibiotic present' grows PURPLE colonies. Beside it, schematic computed-style curves change order when GREEN food labels swap. Clearly label curves 'schematic'; show no numbers.
scenes.narration: Bacteria make the same point. One mutation can allow growth with an antibiotic. Yet with different food, which mutant grows best can change. Food and the drug are both parts of the environment.

scenes.tts: Human examples differ too. Continued lactase production can help where adults drink milk. A dry-earwax change has no survival effect shown in this lesson's evidence. These cases test different traits under different conditions.
scenes.caption: Human examples differ too. Continued lactase production can help where adults drink milk. A dry-earwax change has no survival effect shown in this lesson's evidence. These cases test different traits under different conditions.
scenes.visual: Two panels slide from the bacterial world. Left: an adult silhouette, a milk cup, and a working block labelled 'lactase', with condition 'where adults drink milk'. Right: two ear icons labelled 'wet' and 'dry' beside a neutral gauge reading 'no survival effect shown'.
scenes.narration: Human examples differ too. Continued lactase production can help where adults drink milk. A dry-earwax change has no survival effect shown in this lesson's evidence. These cases test different traits under different conditions.

scenes.tts: Effect and inheritance are separate questions. In animals that reproduce with eggs and sperm, a helpful body-cell mutation still cannot reach offspring. A sex-cell mutation can pass without being helpful. Usefulness cannot open a blocked inheritance route.
scenes.caption: Effect and inheritance are separate questions. In animals that reproduce with eggs and sperm, a helpful body-cell mutation still cannot reach offspring. A sex-cell mutation can pass without being helpful. Usefulness cannot open a blocked inheritance route.
scenes.visual: Return to the parent route map from the first film. Put a small effect gauge beside each GOLD mark. The body-cell path remains blocked RED regardless of its gauge. The sex-cell path remains possible regardless of its gauge.
scenes.narration: Effect and inheritance are separate questions. In animals that reproduce with eggs and sperm, a helpful body-cell mutation still cannot reach offspring. A sex-cell mutation can pass without being helpful. Usefulness cannot open a blocked inheritance route.

scenes.tts: So do not judge a mutation from its name alone. Compare the changed trait, the environment, survival, and reproduction. Evidence decides the effect in that setting. Without those comparisons, the label is only a guess.
scenes.caption: So do not judge a mutation from its name alone. Compare the changed trait, the environment, survival, and reproduction. Evidence decides the effect in that setting. Without those comparisons, the label is only a guess.
scenes.visual: Four large connected panels fill the frame: PURPLE changed trait, GREEN environment, WHITE survival gauge, and WHITE offspring count. A magnifying glass moves across them in order. The GOLD mutation card stays above all four.
scenes.narration: So do not judge a mutation from its name alone. Compare the changed trait, the environment, survival, and reproduction. Evidence decides the effect in that setting. Without those comparisons, the label is only a guess.

scenes.caption: The tables below give that evidence. Use them to separate what changed from the conditions in which scientists tested it. The text also gives limits that this picture cannot carry.
